About

I'm Jiwon Lee, a PhD Candidate in Industrial Design at KAIST . I research and build interactive systems that sit between people and AI — conversational agents, storytelling interfaces, and design tools that scaffold creative thought.

Recurring concerns in my work: how AI-mediated encounters shape memory and anticipation (e.g., embodied future-self agents), how stories surface from mundane data (e.g., dashcam footage), and how grids and graphs let designers externalize tacit reasoning.

Before KAIST, I studied Service & Design Engineering at Sungshin Women's University. In 2024 my undergraduate thesis project was named a Korea National Winner of the James Dyson Award and reached the International Top 20.
